feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the public-sector specialization comes through well. It reads polished and modern, but it is slightly dense and repetitive, with some opportunities to sharpen impact through tighter formatting and more outcome-focused phrasing.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and platform scope over time.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, named tools/platforms.  
- Well-aligned positioning for digital platform, governance, analytics, and communications leadership in complex organizations.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap heavily and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity/scope: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, adoption improvements, cost savings, or campaign results.  
- Fix minor style/consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation is inconsistent across bullets; “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is stylistically unusual unless intentional; “French (A2/Learning)” would read more cleanly as “French (A2, learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning and relevant scope, but the intro is slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with sharper outcomes and a clearer emphasis on recent leadership focus.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years’ experience leading public-sector web platforms, governance, and content operations at scale.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more active, senior language such as “leading enterprise web modernization, analytics, and editorial systems.”
- Add scale or context already supported by the CV, e.g. “high-volume, mission-driven organizations” or “large public-facing platforms.”
- Consider a cleaner rewrite: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years’ experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled digital experiences that improve discovery, coordination, and audience engagement.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; keep it brief here.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely echoes multiple skills sections; avoid listing too many capability areas in the intro.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened into broader, less repetitive capability areas with more parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consolidate overlapping items and use consistent noun phrases; e.g.: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Consider replacing “content experiences” with “content discovery” or “user experience” for clearer meaning.
- Use “public-sector advocacy communications” instead of “advocacy and public-sector communications” for smoother phrasing.
- If space is tight, reduce to 6 themes by merging multimedia with multi-channel operations and governance with workflow systems.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” “AI-enabled…” and “multimedia production” repeat language already used in the header.
- This section also overlaps substantially with Topline Skills; keep one high-level and the other more tool-/function-specific.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tighten wording, standardize style, and frame these as selected examples with clearer outcomes or scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Retitle as “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each entry to one crisp line with parallel verb structure.
- Add specificity where possible: audience, platform, scale, or business purpose (for example, legislative content discovery, campaign growth, conference activation).
- Standardize style: use “AI-enabled,” “Drupal 10,” and “10 x 20-foot”; consider “bill-level chat” instead of “bill-level AI chat” for smoother phrasing.
- Emphasize the most recent freelance work first and keep older NACo-era examples shorter.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video work substantially overlap with Work Experience bullets; this footer should summarize, not restate.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” may also echo broader campaign/storytelling language already present in the consultant role.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope and good alignment to your headline, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and the most distinctive work so it complements—not repeats—your NACo leadership roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; e.g. combine digital systems/workflows/analytics and governance/usability/operations into one operations-improvement bullet.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, publishing speed, search relevance gains, toolkit downloads, stakeholder teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” overlaps heavily with the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize what is new here: consulting model, AI search, Drupal microsites, and hands-on implementation.
- Footer project examples already cover the microsite and AI search—keep this entry higher-level unless you add results.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground enterprise ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo roles on newsletters, video, and day-to-day channel management.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s enterprise digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to emphasize outcomes and scope: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more measurable where possible: add budget size, team size, reporting cadence, production volume, engagement growth, cost savings, or turnaround improvements.
- Combine lower-value bullets: merge analytics + governance into one operational-improvement bullet to save space and keep focus on strategic wins.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry at the enterprise/leadership level.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with earlier video-production bullets; frame it as capacity-building and organizational scale, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like responsibilities than achievements. Tighten it to emphasize scope, channel ownership, and the systems/editorial improvements that set up the later director-level impact.

Suggested edit
- Open with progression + scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Combine newsletters into one sharper bullet: “Owned production of four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-focused: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a repeatable policy communications channel.”
- Rephrase the last two bullets into one stronger systems statement: “Built tighter editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with both the earlier NACo role and Recent Projects; keep the emphasis here on establishing the channel, not production details.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strategically in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent roles. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around senior leadership strengths rather than generic communications language.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording tied to recent work:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy & campaign planning
- Use “cross-channel” instead of “multi-channel” for a more current, integrated feel.
- Swap “messaging” for “communications” or “strategy” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- Keep all bullets parallel noun phrases; avoid vague wording like “audience-focused,” which is weaker than “audience-centered content strategy.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already covered in the header and multiple NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the most relevant recent strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize recent, proven strengths from current/NACo work: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and integrations; demote older or less evidenced platforms.
- Consider removing one lower-priority platform (e.g. SharePoint or Power Pages) unless it is important for target roles.
- If space allows, sharpen with outcome language: “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “Scalable content and publishing systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave full tool inventory below.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic capability and business impact over repeating platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to outcome-oriented capability cluster, e.g.:
- Analytics strategy and KPI design
- Executive and leadership reporting
- GA4, BigQuery, Power BI and Looker Studio dashboards
- User behavior insights, SEO and performance optimization
- Consider dropping one lower-priority tool here (for example Microsoft Clarity) if space is tight; keep the strongest enterprise stack.
- Use parallel phrasing: mix of strategy + reporting + platforms + optimization, not all nouns/tools.
- If possible, align wording to recent impact from NACo: analytics infrastructure, decision support, and performance improvement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly duplicative of “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; Topline Skills should be more strategic, while Technical + IT holds the full tool list.
- “Leadership reporting” may overlap with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; “Executive reporting” is tighter and more specific.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value delivery capabilities rather than tool-level tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to outcome-oriented capability line: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera direction and multi-camera workflows”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the NACo studio build and leadership-level scope.
- Consider dropping “virtual” since “hybrid event delivery” already implies it; this saves space and reduces repetition.
- If accurate, add scale/context instead of generic terms, e.g. “Livestream and hybrid event production for advocacy, conferences and recurring programming.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; vary wording here or remove one instance.
- Tool-specific detail like “PTZ camera systems” may fit better under Technical + IT unless this is a differentiating specialty.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is central to recent work, lead with it and add light qualifiers that signal level of use and modernization scope.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Put the strongest, most recent platform first; Drupal should clearly anchor the list given the 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work.
- Standardize naming: use **Microsoft Power Pages** instead of just Power Pages for clarity and ATS matching.
- If space allows, add proficiency cues only where meaningful, e.g. **Drupal (primary)** rather than qualifying every platform.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the “Topline Skills” web platforms line; consider trimming one of the two or making this version more technical/platform-specific.
- Avoid adding CMS modernization here unless it remains removed from the Topline Skills section.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and tools that support recent, higher-impact work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI-CD**
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used consistently elsewhere; **HTML/CSS** is cleaner.
- If accurate, add one specificity cue tied to recent work, e.g. **front-end troubleshooting for Drupal sites**, **tag deployment**, or **serverless scripting**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations** already appears in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing in both places.
- “Workflow automation” is covered elsewhere, so keep this item focused on coding/implementation tools rather than broader systems.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere. Make it more purposeful by grouping tools by function and emphasizing systems-building over basic collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light functional framing instead of a flat list: **Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams**
- Consider dropping 1–2 lower-value tools if space is tight; keep the platforms most tied to recent systems/governance work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams/Basecamp are common collaboration tools and may dilute impact unless they are central to your recent work.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too bare and undersells your recent leadership in email operations. It should signal enterprise-scale platform ownership and audience engagement without repeating newsletter achievements already covered in work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Replace with: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email campaign operations • Audience segmentation • Journey automation**
- If accurate, strengthen further with one outcome-oriented qualifier: **enterprise newsletter and member communications platforms** or **high-volume advocacy and membership communications**
- Keep product names first, then capabilities; avoid slash-heavy phrasing for cleaner scanning

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Don’t restate “newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in NACo experience bullets
- Avoid adding generic “multi-channel communications,” which is already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Tighten it into a sharper technical list and emphasize methods/tools rather than broad capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting**
- Replace **SEO** with a more concrete tool or practice, e.g. **Google Search Console**, **technical SEO**, or **performance analysis**
- Replace **Dashboarding** with a more outcome-oriented term like **KPI reporting**, **executive dashboards**, or **analytics reporting**
- If truthful, consider adding one higher-signal implementation skill already supported by experience, such as **analytics infrastructure**, **tagging strategy**, or **conversion tracking**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider shortening one of the two or making this version strictly tool-based
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the NACo role, so avoid repeating explanatory detail here

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content execution, and any scale or frequency metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten scope and use parallel verbs: “improved workflows across web, email, social and video; supported a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: website traffic, livestream/event volume, video cadence, email/social growth, or team size.
- Clarify supervision modestly: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “oversaw daily work of…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; if that series continued there, frame this entry as launching or piloting it.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already used more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project support, and trim broad phrases like “contributed to.”

Suggested edit
- Recast to foreground the standout outcome: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research coordination and multimedia communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast.”
- Replace vague verbs with ownership language: “Managed planning, scripting, guest coordination, and production for the organization’s first podcast.”
- Tighten the first sentence to show scope: “Coordinated research and innovation projects that informed program development and policy work.”
- If possible, add one metric or concrete output: number of episodes, stakeholders interviewed, projects supported, or content pieces produced.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles; keep this item focused on podcast launch and research/program support.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream language here since stronger, more recent examples appear in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tightening it into clearer tool categories will make it scan faster and reduce overlap with the stronger “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” skills section.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream production/studio operations • Podcast recording, editing & production**
- Use parallel phrasing: keep software as tools and production abilities as capabilities; avoid vague wording like “workflows.”
- If accurate, add one higher-value tool or system tied to recent work (for example, streaming platform, switcher, or audio setup) instead of generic production terms.
- Consider renaming the heading to **Multimedia Tools & Production** to better match the mix of software and operational skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” overlaps with Topline Skills: “Livestreaming • Studio operations.”
- “Podcast production” is already supported by older experience; keep it brief so recent digital/platform leadership remains the focus.
